name: r26b_4rotor
source: Mazda R26B four-rotor racing rotary (Mazda 787B, Le Mans 1991). CITED: (a) SAE 920309, Shimizu/Tadokoro/Nakanishi/Funamoto (Mazda), 'Mazda 4-Rotor Rotary Engine for the Le Mans 24-Hour Endurance Race' (http://www.mulsannescorner.com/SAE920309.pdf), Table 1: 4-rotor in-line, 654 cc x 4, eccentricity x generating radius x width = 15 x 105 x 80 mm, compression 10.0, 515 kW at 9000 rpm, 608 N*m at 6500 rpm, ignition sequence 1-3-2-4 at 90 deg spacing; (b) Mazda global site (https://www.mazda.com/en/experience/mspr/motorsports/lemans/r26b/): 654 cc x 4, 700 PS at 9000 rpm, 62 kg*m at 6500 rpm; (c) Wikipedia 'Mazda 787B' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazda_787B): 2616 cc, 608 N*m at 6500 rpm, 700 hp at 9000 rpm, and a 650 hp figure at a restricted 8500 rpm; (d) rx7.net.nz R26B page (https://www.rx7.net.nz/r26b.html): 700 bhp at 9000 rpm, called its redline. WOT CURVE: 4000-9000 rpm digitised in 250 rpm steps from SAE 920309 Fig. 6 (the power-oriented full-load torque curve; pixel calibration rpm = 4000 + 1000*(x - 192.5)/75.4, torque = 700 - 300*(y - 344)/223 N*m); the digitised 6500 rpm point (604.5) is replaced by the cited 608 and the digitised 9000 rpm point (536.5) by the cited power, 515000 W / (9000*2*pi/60 rad/s) = 546.4 N*m. Fig. 6 has no data below 4000 rpm: the 500-3500 rpm points are a LINEAR EXTRAPOLATION of the digitised 4000-4500 rpm slope (0.07 N*m/rpm), not data. LIMITER: fuel_cut at 9000 rpm (the rpm of the cited peak power and the end of Fig. 6; source (d) calls it the redline; source (c)'s 8500 rpm is a restricted race setting, not used). MOTORING TORQUE (derivation, no rotary motoring data found): the same Heywood-style SI friction correlation and closed-throttle pumping term used by data/engines/i4_2l_na.json, fmep = 0.97 + 0.15(N/1000) + 0.05(N/1000)^2 bar plus 0.9 bar pumping (0 rpm value = the 0.97 bar Coulomb part only), scaled by the displacement swept per eccentric-shaft revolution: each rotor completes one 654 cc working cycle per shaft revolution (Wikipedia 'Wankel engine': one power pulse per output-shaft revolution per rotor), so 4 x 654 cc = 2616 cc per revolution and torque per bar = 1e5 Pa * 2.616e-3 m^3 / (2*pi) = 41.63 N*m/bar (check: the cited 608 N*m is 14.6 bar bmep on that basis). This is a piston-engine correlation applied by displacement equivalence, not a rotary measurement. INERTIA (derivation): rotor mass 4.328 kg = Mazdatrix rotor chart value for the 1989-92 13B rotor incl. bearing (https://mazdatrix.com/rotor-weight-and-compression-chart/), used because the 13B has the same 15 x 105 x 80 mm rotor geometry as the R26B per source (a) - the R26B's own rotor mass is not cited. A rotor orbits at eccentricity e = 0.015 m at shaft speed and spins at 1/3 shaft speed (Wikipedia 'Wankel engine': one rotor revolution per three shaft revolutions), so its inertia referred to the shaft is m*e^2 + J_spin/9; J_spin approximated as a solid equilateral triangle of circumradius R = 0.105 m, J = m*R^2/4 = 0.01193 kg*m^2. Per rotor 4.328*0.015^2 + 0.01193/9 = 0.000974 + 0.001326 = 0.00230; four rotors 0.0092 kg*m^2. Plus an ASSUMED 0.05 kg*m^2 (not cited) for the eccentric shaft, balance weights, flywheel and clutch pressure plate/cover; total 0.0592, rounded to 0.06. BREAKAWAY 50 N*m: assumed, chosen just above the loader's minimum (-motoring(0) = 40.4 N*m). IDLE: no published R26B idle speed was found; idle_rpm 1500 is ASSUMED, stall/fire/start_complete/dfco thresholds assumed around it. Idle PI gains: i4_2l_na.json's kp/ki divided by 5.83, the ratio of (d torque/d throttle)/inertia at idle between the two engines ((254 + 92.4)/0.06) / ((128 + 30.4)/0.16) (i4_2l_na: WOT 128 and motoring -30.4 N*m at its 800 rpm idle, interpolated from its own curves), so the idle loop keeps the same closed-loop poles; max_throttle 0.4 because the feed-forward idle throttle -m/(w - m) at 1500 rpm is 92.4/346.4 = 0.267. Starter values assumed (initial_state running; not used by any test).
